rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate all eight peaks and identify critical separations while minimizing the risk of missing retained compounds. A midpoint temperature leaves room to adjust selectivity in either direction.

Only the first pair limits the score, so test whether higher temperature improves its selectivity while keeping the gradient unchanged. The other pairs have resolution margin, and higher temperature should keep the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes.

Keep the favorable temperature and make the gradient one step shallower to improve the first pair from R = 1.41 toward full resolution. The last peak at 6.56 minutes leaves ample room to lengthen the gradient without a time penalty.

Injection 3 reached the maximum CRF; now seek a shorter fully resolved method. This gradient has a slope between injections 2 and 3, which should retain R ≥ 1.5 for the first pair while bringing the last peak out earlier.

Test a higher starting fraction to shorten retention, with a slightly shallower slope to protect the first pair. The final fraction remains above the last peak’s estimated elution fraction of 0.57, so all peaks should remain within the gradient.

Restore the lower starting fraction and test a slope between injections 2 and 4, targeting first-pair resolution just above 1.5 with earlier final elution. The last peak may elute shortly into the final hold; injection 4 remains the fully resolved fallback.

Reduce the slope relative to injection 5 to recover full resolution of the first pair at the higher starting fraction. This tests whether a trimmed solvent window can preserve maximum CRF with a shorter method than injection 3.

Maximum CRF is already secured, so test the unexplored low-temperature limit for an alternative selectivity window. Comparing this with injections 1 and 2 will show whether cooling separates the critical pair in the opposite elution order.

Test whether a steeper gradient breaks up the low-temperature late-peak cluster while retaining the first pair’s resolution margin. This also shortens retention substantially, probing an alternative route to a faster fully resolved separation.

The late cluster barely responded to slope at 25 C, so increase temperature to change its selectivity. An intermediate gradient duration should preserve more first-pair resolution than the six-minute gradient while testing a potentially faster separation.

Raise temperature to separate the late cluster and shift the starting fraction to test first-pair selectivity in this cooler regime. The higher start should also shorten the run, potentially revealing a faster fully resolved alternative to the 60 C methods.

At 35 C the late cluster is resolved, leaving only the first pair to improve. Lower the starting fraction and use a shallower gradient to spread that pair, targeting another maximum-CRF method with the last peak still below 10 minutes.

Test whether a higher starting fraction can shorten the fully resolved 35 C separation while retaining a slope close to injection 12. This probes starting-composition selectivity of the first pair, with the late cluster already showing adequate resolution at this temperature.

Return to the faster 60 C regime with a slope slightly shallower than injection 6 to add first-pair resolution margin. The higher endpoint keeps the last peak inside the gradient, targeting maximum CRF with final elution near seven minutes.

Test a small slope increase beyond injection 6 to locate the fastest fully resolved boundary. This should bring the last peak out slightly earlier, although the first pair may fall just below R = 1.5; injection 6 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

The fastest full-resolution boundary is now bracketed by injections 6 and 15. With maximum CRF secured, test a shallower gradient for greater resolution margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Test a slope between injections 5 and 7 to approach the full-resolution boundary at phi0 = 0.10. This should preserve approximately R = 1.5 for the first pair while shortening retention relative to injection 7.

Test a further increase in starting organic fraction with a shallower gradient to compensate for the first pair’s loss of resolution. This probes whether trimming more of the initial solvent window can retain maximum CRF while keeping final elution below 10 minutes.

Refine the successful phi0 = 0.10 method with a shallower slope to add resolution margin above injection 17’s borderline first pair. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, preserving maximum CRF while testing a less marginal separation.

Shorten injection 19 by one gradient-time step to trade excess resolution for speed. Its slope will be slightly shallower than the fully resolved injection 17, so maximum CRF should be retained with final elution near 7.2 minutes.

Test a narrower endpoint window at the successful low starting fraction, targeting more first-pair resolution margin than injection 14. The last peak should remain within the gradient and below 10 minutes, preserving maximum CRF with an eight-minute programmed gradient.

Test a slightly lower operating temperature with a shallower gradient to compensate for reduced first-pair selectivity. This seeks a maximum-score alternative below 60 C while keeping the last peak within the ten-minute scoring window.

Return to 60 C and preserve injection 3’s successful gradient slope while shortening the programmed gradient to eight minutes. The endpoint remains above the last peak’s estimated elution fraction, so this should retain full resolution and maximum CRF.

Preserve injection 23’s successful slope but end the gradient two minutes earlier, testing a lower-solvent final hold. The early separations should remain unchanged; the key check is whether the last compound still elutes before 10 minutes, preserving maximum CRF.

Use the final injection to test a trimmed version of injection 16 with nearly the same slope, targeting minimum resolution near 1.9 and final elution below nine minutes. This should retain maximum CRF with more separation margin than the fastest confirmed method, injection 6.
